newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-ITALY SEIZE UNDERDOG ROLE AGAINST SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ITALY SEIZE UNDERDOG ROLE AGAINST SPAIN.

text.p: Italy's Davis Cup captain Adriano Panatta is doing his best to lull Spain into a false sense of security on the eve of his country's second round tie in the Adriatic beach resort of Pesaro.

Panatta claimed his side were unlikely to extend the indoor tie into the final day on Sunday and, publicly at least, has all but written off Italy's chances of beating a Spanish team featuring two players in the world's top 20.
"Sunday? No, it will already be decided by then," Corriere dello Sport quoted Panatta as saying.
"They have an 80 percent chance of winning and we have 20 percent. That seems to me a realistic forecast," he added.
Panatta's words will be put to the test on Friday's opening match, when veteran Omar Camporese takes on Spain's Carlos Moya, ranked eighth in the world.
Italy did have some good news on Wednesday when their number one Renzo Furlan, the mainstay of the squad, was given the green light for the singles after recovering from a thigh injury.
Furlan, ranked 64 in the world, faces 12th ranked Albert Costa in the second singles tie on Friday.
Camporese and Diego Nargiso will then meet Francis Roig and Javier Sanchez in the doubles on Saturday.
But Spanish coach Santana, who has won Wimbledon, the U.S. and French Opens, was careful not to write off the Italians.
"If Camporese finds his strokes he can put any opponent in difficulty. As for Furlan, he is a player of exceptional consistency who always gives everything," he said.

Spain have never won the Davis Cup but are widely expected to do well this year. Italy won the competition once in 1976. The two sides have met nine times previously in the cup, with Italy winning six times and Spain three.
